change_interpretations.engineering_summary: position demand >70% has been relaxed from 100 ms to 120 ms. Existing pass evidence within 100 ms remains valid, but test scripts and procedures with explicit 100 ms thresholds require updating.

assessments.reason: TV-001 directly tests accelerator torque response at 75% demand under VCU-DR-01. The measured 94 ms result satisfies the relaxed 120 ms limit, but the procedure and script threshold of 100 ms must be updated.
assessments.recommended_action: Update the procedure and test script pass/fail threshold from 100 ms to 120 ms.

assessments.reason: TV-002 links to VCU-DR-01 and applies 85% pedal demand, but its primary procedure verifies command priorities under VCU-BRK-03. The relaxation of VCU-DR-01 response time to 120 ms does not alter brake override priority behavior.
evidence: inspect torque and pressure command priorities
Timing not reported in old evidence
assessments.recommended_action: No immediate change needed; verify if torque response timing during arbitration needs explicit tracking in future campaigns.

assessments.reason: TV-003 sweeps pedal demand above 70% (75–95%) and records response latency, directly testing VCU-DR-01 behavior despite the missing requirement link. The measured maximum of 92 ms remains compliant with 120 ms, but the legacy tolerance check of 95 ms requires alignment.
evidence: Legacy suite still checks 95 ms tolerance
assessments.recommended_action: Update the legacy test procedure and script tolerance check from 95 ms to 120 ms.

assessments.reason: TV-004 measures emergency brake actuator response latency under VCU-BRK-03. As confirmed in workshop notes, brake command latency uses a different measurement clock and must not be conflated with positive torque response under VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Brake command latency and positive torque command latency are measured by different clocks

assessments.reason: TV-005 verifies wheel-speed sensor degradation behavior under VCU-DGN-04, which is unchanged and unrelated to driver torque response time.
TV-006 checks logging of operating mode transitions under VCU-LOG-05, which is unaffected by changes to VCU-DR-01 torque response timing.
evidence: Change Comfort to Sport; log timestamp

assessments.reason: TV-007 exercises 80% pedal demand (above the 70% threshold of VCU-DR-01) but has a TBD link, unassigned ownership, and was never executed. Human review is required to confirm requirement traceability and execution plans.
evidence: Ownership and source link to be clarified
assessments.recommended_action: Request that the engineering owner clarify requirement mapping, assign test ownership, and determine execution scope.

assessments.reason: TV-008 replays legacy diagnostic traces and does not evaluate driver accelerator torque response time under VCU-DR-01.
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for this specification change.

assessments.reason: TV-009 compares torque ramp profiles between Sport and Comfort modes under VCU-MOD-06 and contains no quantitative response-time assertion for VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Compare accelerator response under Sport vs Comfort

assessments.reason: TV-010 verifies pedal signal spike filtering under VCU-DR-02, which remains unchanged and distinct from VCU-DR-01 torque response timing.
TV-011 tests torque reduction during emergency braking under VCU-BRK-03, which is unchanged and independent of VCU-DR-01 response time relaxation.
evidence: While demand is high, request emergency braking

assessments.reason: TV-012 measures ECU platform readiness latency after power cycle, which is unrelated to accelerator torque response under VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Power cycle the ECU; verify readiness within 500 ms
